newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rally, look to rosy January.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rally, look to rosy January.

text.p: Argentine bonds rallied again late Friday as the market flew higher on positive momentum and on prospects for more gains in January.
"The bond market has been very firm," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, senior analyst at financial consultancy C&E Consultores.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.70 at 123.80, while the FRB due 2005 rose 3/8 to 87-3/8.
Traders said activity was still thin after Christmas, but noted that more players were gradually returning to the market.
Traders said the market was boosted this session by a solid rise in U.S. Treasuries.
"Treasury bond gains have created a breakout above 87-1/8 (in the FRB)," said analysts at MMS International in an investor note.

Dealers are looking with increasing optimism to the first quarter of 1997 as the favorable factors that helped the market in 1996, notably low U.S. rates, are seen continuing in the new year, said traders.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 8.0 percent from 7.38 percent.
